'''Sir Richard Henry Treisman''' (born 7 October 1954)<ref name=whoswho/> is a British scientist specialising in the [[molecular biology]] of cancer. Treisman is a director of research at the [[Francis Crick Institute]] in London.

==Education==
Treisman was educated at [[Haberdashers' Aske's Boys' School]]<ref name=whoswho/> and [[Christ's College, Cambridge]], where he was awarded a Bachelor of Arts degree in 1977.<ref name=whoswho/> He completed his postgraduate study at the [[London Research Institute|Imperial Cancer Research Fund]] (ICRF) and [[University College London]], where he was awarded a PhD for research on [[Polyomaviridae|polyomavirus]] transcription and [[RNA]] processing supervised by Bob Kamen<ref name=blue/> in 1981.<ref>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University College London (University of London)|title=The structures of polyoma virus-specific nuclear and cytoplasmic RNA molecules|first= Richard Henry|last=Treisman|year=1981|url=http://catalogue.libraries.london.ac.uk/record=b1523865|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.290828}}|oclc=556387169|website=london.ac.uk}}</ref>

==Career and research==
After his PhD, Treisman pursued [[postdoctoral research]] at [[Harvard University]] on [[globin]] gene expression and [[thalassemia]] genes with [[Tom Maniatis]]. In 1984, he joined the [[Medical Research Council (United Kingdom)|Medical Research Council]] (MRC) [[Laboratory of Molecular Biology]] (LMB) at the [[University of Cambridge]], where he started working on how [[growth factor]]s control transcription. Initially focusing on the [[c-Fos|Fos gene]], he identified the [[transcription factor]] [[Serum response factor]] (SRF) and cloned its gene, before returning to London in 1988.<ref name=frs>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/richard-treisman-12432/|title=Richard Treisman|website=royalsociety.org|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20171027224902/https://royalsociety.org/people/richard-treisman-12432/|archivedate=27 October 2017|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|author=Anon|location=London|year=1994|accessdate=27 May 2018}} One or more of the preceding sentences incorporates text from the royalsociety.org website where: {{blockquote|"All text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]]." --{{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161111170346/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/|title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies|date=2016-11-11}}}}</ref>

He showed that the [[TCF/LEF family|TCF family]] of SRF [[Cofactor (biochemistry)|cofactors]] are targets for [[Mitogen-activated protein kinase]] (MAPK) signalling, and demonstrated that the MRTF transcription cofactors are novel [[G-actin]] binding proteins that sense fluctuations in G-actin concentration. He continues to focus on SRF's regulatory cofactors and their cognate signalling pathways.<ref name=frs/>

Treisman was Director of the [[Cancer Research UK]] (CRUK) [[London Research Institute]] from 2000 to 2015, becoming Research Director of the Francis Crick Institute in 2009.

===Awards and honours===
Treisman was elected a member of the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] in 1988<ref name=membo/> and a [[Fellow of the Academy of Medical Sciences]] (FMedSci) in 2000;<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr. Richard Treisman |url=https://acmedsci.ac.uk/fellows/fellows-directory/ordinary-fellows/fellow/Richard%20Henry-Treisman-0033z00002qIIWbAAO |access-date=2026-07-12 |website=The Academy of Medical Sciences |language=en}}</ref> he received the [[EMBO Gold Medal]] in 1995<ref name=gold>{{Cite journal|last=Treisman|first=Richard|year=1995|title=Journey to the surface of the cell: Fos regulation and the SRE | journal=[[The EMBO Journal]]|volume=14|issue=20|pages=4905–4913 |pmc=394592|pmid=7588619 |doi=10.1002/j.1460-2075.1995.tb00173.x}}</ref> and the [[Louis-Jeantet Prize for Medicine]] in 2002.<ref name="Louis-Jeantet Prize">[https://www.jeantet.ch/en/prix-louis-jeantet/laureats/2002-en/docteur-richard-treisman/ Louis-Jeantet Prize]</ref> He was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 1994|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 1994]] and knighted in the [[2016 Birthday Honours]].<ref name=sir>{{London Gazette |issue= 61608 |date=11 June 2016 |page=B2}}</ref><ref name=bbc>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/health-36499807|publisher=BBC|title=Birthday honours: Mitochondrial disease doctor recognised|year=2016|author=Anon}}</ref>
